consumer_interfaces.current_statement:
Let $z_0\in[0,1)$ and define $f:(-\infty,1)\to\mathbb R$ by $f(z):=(1-z)^{-1/2}=\bigl((1-z)^{1/2}\bigr)^{-1}$, the reciprocal of the nonnegative square root, with rational powers as in [[def-rational-power]]; put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$.

(a) $f$ is differentiable on $(-\infty,1)$ with $f'(z)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$, and twice differentiable there with $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$; in particular $|f''(z)|\le\tfrac34(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$ for every $z\in[0,z_0]$.

(b) For every $z\in[0,z_0]$ there is a real $R(z)$ with $$f(z)=1+\tfrac z2+R(z),\qquad |R(z)|\le K(z_0)\,z^2,$$ so $|f(z)-1|\le\tfrac z2+K(z_0)z^2$ for $z\in[0,z_0]$. Consequently, for every $\eta>0$, $$0\le z\le\min\!\left\{z_0,\frac{\eta}{\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0}\right\}\ \Longrightarrow\ |f(z)-1|\le\eta ;$$ the display is the quantitative form of $f(z)\to1$ as $z\to0^+$ used by [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]].

The lemma is a statement of real analysis about the single function $f$; it attaches no physical meaning to $z$ and makes no claim about a Lorentz factor or a physical velocity.
consumer_interfaces.current_strategy:
(a) Write $f(z)=g(1-z)^{-1}$ with $g(y):=y^{1/2}$ for $y>0$, or directly apply the power rule: by [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]] the rational powers of [[def-rational-power]] agree on rational exponents with the real powers differentiated in [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], whose second clause gives $(x^{\alpha})'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}$ on $(0,\infty)$; the affine map $z\mapsto 1-z$ has derivative the constant $-1$ (identity and sum rules, [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]]), so the chain rule [[thm-chain-rule]] applied to $z\mapsto(1-z)^{-1/2}=y^{\alpha}\circ(1-z)$ with $\alpha=-1/2$ gives $f'(z)=-\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}\cdot(-1)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$, and repeating with $\alpha=-3/2$ gives $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$; the identities $(1-z)^{\alpha}(1-z)^{-\alpha}=1$ and $a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$ are [[lem-rational-power-laws]]. For the bound: from $0\le z\le z_0$ we have $0<1-z_0\le1-z$, so positive-base $5/2$-power monotonicity in the base of [[lem-rational-power-monotone]] with $r=5/2$ gives $(1-z_0)^{5/2}\le(1-z)^{5/2}$ (equality exactly when $z=z_0$, by the strict part otherwise), and [[lem-of-inverse-positive]] gives $(1-z)^{-5/2}\le(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$; multiplying by $\tfrac34$ and reading $|f''|=f''$ (the strict positivity of the power, [[lem-rational-power-laws]] clause 1) gives the claim.

(b) Put $n=1$, $a=0$, $x=z\in[0,z_0]$ in [[cor-taylor-remainder-bound]]: $f$ has derivatives through order $2$ on the closed interval between $0$ and $z$ with endpoint continuity (indeed it is $C^{\infty}$ on the open neighbourhood $(-\infty,1)$ of that interval), and $|f''(t)|\le\tfrac34(1-z_0)^{-5/2}=:M$ there by (a); hence $|R_{1,0}f(z)|\le M z^2/2!=K(z_0)z^2$ for $R(z):=R_{1,0}f(z)=f(z)-f(0)-f'(0)z=f(z)-1-\tfrac z2$. The final display follows from $|f(z)-1|\le z(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z)\le z(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0)$ for $z\le z_0$ and the order arithmetic of $\mathbb R$ with the absolute-value properties of [[lem-of-abs-value]] ([[def-abs-value]]). The final implication explicitly retains z<=z0; its bound is not asserted beyond the original Taylor interval. At z0=0 it applies only to z=0, while the one-sided convergence statement may use any fixed positive z0<1.

consumer_interfaces.current_statement: Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame of the model (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart), and let x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) be its coordinates, so that a vector is written x = x^0 e_0 + x^1 e_1 + x^2 e_2 + x^3 e_3 and the spatial part is the coordinate column x_vec = (x^1,x^2,x^3) of R^3 with its standard Euclidean structure (def-euclidean-inner-product). For beta in R^3 with |beta| < 1, where |beta| is the Euclidean norm, set gamma(beta) := (1 - |beta|^2)^(-1/2) >= 1, with equality exactly for beta=0 and strict inequality for beta!=0 (def-rational-power, lem-rational-power-laws). The passive Lorentz boost with parameter beta is the linear map B(beta): V -> V defined by its action on coordinates: for beta not equal to 0, x'^0 = gamma (x^0 - beta . x),  x' = x + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . x) beta - gamma beta x^0, and for beta = 0, B(0) := identity, where x' denotes the coordinates of B(beta) applied to the vector with coordinates x, and beta . x is the Euclidean scalar product. Equivalently, in the ordered basis (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) the matrix of B(beta) is B^0_0 = gamma, B^0_i = B^i_0 = -gamma beta_i for i = 1,2,3, and B^i_j = delta^i_j + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2) beta_i beta_j for i,j = 1,2,3 (with the last expression replaced by delta^i_j for beta = 0; the coefficient (gamma−1)/|beta|^2 tends to 1/2 as beta tends to0 through nonzero vectors, so the correction is (1/2) beta_i beta_j+o(|beta|^2) and the full spatial block tends to delta^i_j). In the 1+1 case beta = beta e_1 this reads x'^0 = gamma(x^0 - beta x^1), x'^1 = gamma(x^1 - beta x^0). The vector beta is called the boost parameter; it is dimensionless and mathematically independent of any unit convention.

The Euclidean norm convention gives $|\beta_i|^2\le\sum_k\beta_k^2=|\beta|^2$, hence $|\beta_i|\le|\beta|$ and $|\beta_i\beta_j|\le|\beta|^2$. In the norm meaning of $\beta\to0$, $|\beta|\to0$. Together with the already proved spatial-block limit these are every matrix entry of $B(\beta)\to I$.

consumer_interfaces.current_statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $c>0$ with the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and let $m>0$.

(a) For $w\in S$ define the *Newtonian comparison momentum* and the *Newtonian comparison kinetic energy* of the pair $(m,w)$ by $$N_p(m,w):=mw,\qquad N_K(m,w):=\tfrac12\,m\,|w|^2,$$ where $mw$ is the scalar multiple of $w$ by the real number $m$ ([[def-linear-map]]) and $|w|^2=\delta(w,w)$ ([[def-integer-power]]). With the SI conventions these carry the units kilogram metre per second and joule respectively.

(b) Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval ([[def-interval]]) and let $y:I\to A$ have inertial coordinate path $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$; writing $r(t)=r^1(t)e_1+r^2(t)e_2+r^3(t)e_3$ with real functions $r^1,r^2,r^3$, at each parameter value $t$ where all three coordinate derivatives exist, define the *coordinate velocity* $w(t)\in S$ of the path by $$w(t):=(r^1)'(t)\,e_1+(r^2)'(t)\,e_2+(r^3)'(t)\,e_3,$$ the componentwise derivative of [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]. For a path differentiable at every parameter value these are functions on $I$; otherwise they are defined on its differentiability set. The comparison functionals along the path are $t\mapsto N_p(m,w(t))$ and $t\mapsto N_K(m,w(t))$.

(c) The functionals $N_p$ and $N_K$ are comparison expressions built from a named inertial frame, the mass parameter $m$ and the path's coordinate velocity. They are not defined by, and do not presuppose, a separately developed Newtonian theory, and this definition asserts no approximation, correspondence, error bound or physical claim; those are the content of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]].
consumer_interfaces.current_strategy: A definition item. Well-definedness: clause (a) applies the scalar multiple of a vector of the real vector space $V$ (restricted to $S\subseteq V$) and the square of the norm $|\cdot|$ supplied by the frame's spatial structure, both total on $S$; clause (b) uses the componentwise derivative of a function $I\to\mathbb R^3$ and the unique expansion of a vector of $S$ in the ordered basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]. No division occurs and no choice is used. The definition deliberately introduces no physical correspondence: it only names the two expressions that [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] compares with the model's measured quantities, and the units are the ones fixed by [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. The derivative symbols in(b) are used only at points where the coordinate derivatives exist; no velocity is assigned to an arbitrary nondifferentiable path. Physical correspondence consumers retain their stated differentiable future-timelike worldline hypotheses.

consumer_interfaces.current_statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model and let $c>0$ be a fixed mathematical speed scale, with the coordinate convention $x^0=ct$, let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x$ and spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and write the points of $\mathbb R\times S$ as $(t,x)$.

(a) *Lorentz boost charts with a variable speed scale.* For $v\in S$ and a real $C>|v|$ put $\gamma_C(v):=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[def-rational-power]]) and define the affine map $\Phi_{v,C}:\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R\times S$ by $$\Phi_{v,C}(t,x):=\Bigl(\gamma_C(v)\bigl(t-\tfrac{\delta(v,x)}{C^2}\bigr),\ \ x+\tfrac{\gamma_C(v)-1}{|v|^2}\delta(v,x)\,v-\gamma_C(v)\,t\,v\Bigr)\quad(v\ne0),$$ with $\Phi_{0,C}:=\mathrm{id}$; when $|v|<c$, at $C=c$ this is the coordinate expression, in the convention $x^0=ct$, of the passive Lorentz boost $B(v/c)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: if an event has coordinates $(ct,x)$ in the unprimed inertial chart of the frame, then $\Phi_{v,c}(t,x)$ are its coordinates $(x'^0/c,\,x'^1,x'^2,x'^3)$ in the boosted inertial chart with parameter $v/c$.

(b) *Galilean boost.* For $v\in S$ define the affine map $G_v:\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R\times S$ by $G_v(t,x):=(t,\,x-tv)$.

(c) *Bounded chart region.* For reals $T,R>0$ put $D_{T,R}:=\{(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S:|t|\le T,\ |x|\le R\}$, with $|\cdot|$ the norm of the named frame.

(d) *Scope of the family.* The parameter $C$ is a variable speed scale inside a family of coordinate expressions; it is not a change of the model's adopted constant $c$, and the members with $C\ne c$ are auxiliary mathematical maps used only to state the limit of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]. Nothing here asserts a physical limit of the framework, and no limiting trajectory, force or interaction is defined.
consumer_interfaces.current_strategy: A definition item. Well-definedness: for $v\ne0$, $C>|v|$ the number $\gamma_C(v)$ is a rational power of the positive base $1-|v|^2/C^2$ ([[def-rational-power]]), and the displayed formulas assign to each pair $(t,x)$ a pair of elements of $\mathbb R\times S$ using the bilinear form $\delta$ and scalar multiplication in $S$; for $v=0$ the middle term is $0/0$ and the map is declared separately to be the identity (the same convention as [[def-lorentz-boost]]). The identification at $C=c$ is made only when $|v|<c$, so this member belongs to the family; it is a substitution: writing $\beta:=v/c$ and $x^0:=ct$ in the definition of $B(\beta)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]] gives $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta\cdot x)$ and $x'=x+((\gamma-1)/|\beta|^2)(\beta\cdot x)\beta-\gamma\beta x^0$, that is $x'^0/c=\gamma_C(v)(t-\delta(v,x)/C^2)$ and the displayed spatial formula, because $\beta\cdot x=\delta(v,x)/c$, $|\beta|^2=|v|^2/c^2$ and $\beta x^0=(v/c)(ct)=vt$. The definition proves no uniform limit; the purely mathematical bounded-region limit is proved later. It assigns no physical interpretation to the auxiliary family, which varies C without changing the fixed model parameter c.

consumer_interfaces.current_statement: Let B(beta) be the passive boost of def-lorentz-boost in an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3). For every beta in R^3 with |beta| < 1 the following hold. (i) B(beta) is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map: eta(B(beta)v,B(beta)w) = eta(v,w) for all v,w in V, det B(beta) = +1, and B(beta)(C^+) = C^+. (ii) B(0) is the identity, and for every beta the image of the frame vector e_0 is B(beta)e_0 = gamma(e_0 - beta_1 e_1 - beta_2 e_2 - beta_3 e_3), so the map beta |-> B(beta) is injective and B(beta) fixes the origin; moreover for every vector y with coordinates (0,y_vec) and beta . y = 0 one has B(beta)y = y. (iii) B(-beta)B(beta) = B(beta)B(-beta) = identity; in particular B(beta) is invertible with B(beta)^{-1} = B(-beta), and B(beta) and B(-beta) are inverse bijections of V. (iv) If u is a future timelike unit vector with coordinates (u^0,u_vec), so that eta(u,u) = -1 and u^0 > 0, and |u_vec| < u^0, then the boost with parameter beta := u_vec/u^0 satisfies B(beta)u = e_0. (v) If a vector x has x^0 > |x_vec|, then the first coordinate of B(beta)x is gamma(x^0 - beta . x) > 0; if x^0 < -|x_vec| then the first coordinate of B(beta)x is negative. In particular B(beta) maps the future open cone {x^0 > |x_vec|} into itself.

(i) For v = (v^0, v_parallel e + v_perp) and w likewise, eta(Bv,Bw) expands into the P-block computed by matrix multiplication, using gamma^2(1 - b^2) = 1 and gamma^2 b^2 + 1 = gamma^2, plus the P^perp-block and the vanishing of the cross terms (P perpendicular to P^perp); this gives eta(Bv,Bw) = eta(v,w). The determinant is the 2x2 determinant gamma^2(1 - b^2) = 1 times the identity on P^perp, hence +1. For the future cone: beta . x <= b|x_vec| < b x^0 whenever x^0 > |x_vec| >= 0, so x^0 - beta . x > x^0(1 - b) > 0; then B(beta)(C^+) is contained in C^+ (it is contained in the future open cone and connected), and since B(beta) is a Lorentz map with inverse B(-beta) (proved next) that also maps C^+ into C^+, one gets B(beta)(C^+) = C^+. (iii) On P the two matrices multiply to gamma^2(1 - b^2) times the identity, using gamma^2(1 - b^2) = 1; on P^perp both are the identity. Hence B(-beta)B(beta) = B(beta)B(-beta) = identity. consumer_interfaces.current_statement: Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame, let S := span(e_1,e_2,e_3) be its spatial three-space and let L be a proper orthochronous Lorentz map (def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group). Let $v\in S$, $T,R>0$, and let $(\Phi_{v,C})_{C>|v|}$, $G_v$ and $D_{T,R}$ be as in [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]]. For $C>|v|$ write $\gamma_C:=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ and $z:=|v|^2/C^2$, and for $(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S$ write $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)=(t',x')$.

(a) *Exact differences.* For every $C>|v|$ and all $(t,x)$,
$$t'-t=(\gamma_C-1)t-\gamma_C\frac{\delta(v,x)}{C^2},\qquad x'-(x-tv)=(\gamma_C-1)(x_\parallel-tv),$$ where $x_\parallel:=\delta(v,x)v/|v|^2$ for $v\ne0$; for $v=0$ one has $\Phi_{0,C}=\mathrm{id}$ and both differences vanish.

(b) *Uniform bounds on bounded regions.* For every $v\ne0$, every $C>|v|$ and every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$,
$$|t'-t|\le(\gamma_C-1)T+\gamma_C\frac{|v|R}{C^2},\qquad |x'-(x-tv)|\le(\gamma_C-1)(R+|v|T).$$

(c) *Quantitative rate and uniform convergence to the Galilean chart map.* Fix $z_0\in(0,1)$ and set $K_0=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, $A_0=\tfrac12+K_0z_0$ and $\Gamma_0=(1-z_0)^{-1/2}$. Whenever $v\ne0$ and $C\ge |v|/\sqrt{z_0}$, the following hold uniformly on $D_{T,R}$: $$|t'-t|\le\frac{A_0|v|^2T+\Gamma_0|v|R}{C^2},\qquad |x'-(x-tv)|\le\frac{A_0|v|^2(R+|v|T)}{C^2}.$$ Thus the rate is $O(C^{-2})$ with explicit constants for fixed $v,T,R,z_0$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C_\varepsilon>|v|$ such that for every $C\ge C_\varepsilon$ and every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$, $$\max\{|t'-t|,\,|x'-(x-tv)|\}\le\varepsilon .$$ For $v\ne0$, put $H=T+R+|v|T$, choose any $z_1$ with $0<z_1\le\min\{z_0,(2A_0)^{-1},\varepsilon/(2A_0H)\}$ (for example the displayed minimum), and set $$C_\varepsilon=\max\{|v|/\sqrt{z_1},\sqrt{3|v|R/\varepsilon}\}.$$ This is sufficient, and since $z_1<1$ it gives $C_\varepsilon>|v|$. For $v=0$ both errors vanish identically and any $C_\varepsilon>0$ suffices. Hence $\sup_{D_{T,R}}\max\{|t'-t|,|x'-(x-tv)|\}\to0$ as $C\to\infty$ with $v,T,R$ fixed, the convergence is uniform on $D_{T,R}$, and for each fixed $(t,x)$ the image $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)$ converges to the Galilean value $G_v(t,x)=(t,x-tv)$.

(d) *Failure on unbounded regions.* For every $v\ne0$ and every $C>|v|$, $\sup_{\mathbb R\times S}|t'-t|=+\infty$ and $\sup_{\mathbb R\times S}|x'-(x-tv)|=+\infty$; so the boundedness of $T,R$ in (c) is essential and the limit is not uniform on the whole chart domain.

(v) Scope: the theorem concerns the affine Minkowski model with a fixed positive constant c; it is a statement about the weak piecewise C^1 future timelike class, including the ordinary Riemann special case (H), it does not identify proper time with any clock reading, and it asserts nothing about maximality of geodesics in curved spacetimes or in Lorentzian manifolds with different global structure.

consumer_interfaces.current_statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space with the reachability objects <=, <, J^+, I^+ and R^+ of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space. (a) Displacement of a future causal path. Let a < b be real numbers and let x: [a,b] -> A be a piecewise C^1 future causal path with D := x(b) - x(a). Then D is in Cbar^+. If x has a future timelike one-sided tangent at some point of [a,b], then D is in C^+. If x is nonconstant, then D is not 0. (b) Reachability and straight segments. J^+(p) = R^+(p), and for q not p one has q in J^+(p) if and only if the straight path s |-> p + s(q - p), s in [0,1], is a future causal path; moreover I^+(p) = {q : the straight path from p to q is future timelike} = {q : q is reachable from p by a piecewise C^1 future causal path having a future timelike one-sided tangent at some point}, and p is in neither of these two sets. (c) No causal loops. If p <= q and q <= p then p = q; equivalently there is no nonconstant piecewise C^1 future causal path x: [a,b] -> A with x(b) = x(a). (d) Time monotonicity. For the chart x of every inertial frame and every piecewise C^1 future causal path y: [a,b] -> A, the composition x^0 o y is nondecreasing, and if y is nonconstant on a subinterval [a',b'] of [a,b] then (x^0 o y)(b') > (x^0 o y)(a'); in particular every inertial frame agrees that a nonconstant future causal path does not go backwards in coordinate time. (e) Straight-worldline maximum. Let p,q be events with q in I^+(p), put D := q - p and T := sqrt(-eta(D,D)) > 0. Then for every piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline y: [a,b] -> A with y(a) = p and y(b) = q, the elapsed proper time Delta tau(y)=c^{-1} sum_i integral_(a_i,b_i) sqrt(-eta(y',y')), defined by the finite improper-piece sum of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time on the weak C^1 pieces a = a_1 < b_1 = a_2 < ... < b_m = b, is at most T/c; equality holds if and only if the image of y is the straight segment from p to q and y traverses it with a strictly increasing time coordinate, i.e. y is a strictly increasing reparametrization of s |-> p + sD. (f) Invariance. For every proper orthochronous affine Lorentz map F of the model one has F(J^+(p)) = J^+(F(p)) and F(I^+(p)) = I^+(F(p)) for every event p, and p <= q if and only if F(p) <= F(q) for all events p,q. (g) Scope. The theorem concerns the affine model: it attaches no physical interpretation to <=, J^+, I^+ and R^+, asserts nothing about partial differential equations, propagation of particular fields or differentiability beyond piecewise C^1, and uses no choice principle.
consumer_interfaces.current_strategy: Proof in dependency order; (a)-(d) are integral inequalities, (e) is the same inequality after a boost normalization, (f) is the cone invariance of a proper orthochronous Lorentz map. (a) Fix an inertial chart. By lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability, all coordinate derivatives are absolutely improperly integrable and their finite sums equal D, with D0>=|D_spatial|. The lemma's strictness clause covers both an interior timelike tangent and a timelike one-sided quotient tangent at a corner, without derivative-limit continuity. A regular future causal path has D0>0; more generally D0=0 implies every nonnegative interior time derivative is zero: any positive value would by continuity have a compact positive neighborhood and force a positive time increment. Then |z'|<=y0'=0 on every open piece, so every coordinate is constant on the pieces and endpoint continuity makes the complete path constant. This repairs the D0=0 inference explicitly; spatial vanishing alone does not prove time vanishing. (b) q in J^+(p) with q not p means D in Cbar^+ with D not 0; the straight path s |-> p + sD has constant tangent D (def-derivative, def-affine-space-and-displacement), which is future causal and nonzero, so it is a future causal path; conversely a future causal straight path has nonzero future causal tangent D, so D is in Cbar^+; this proves R^+(p) = J^+(p) and the straight-segment criterion. For I^+(p): if D is in C^+, the straight path is a future causal path with future timelike tangent, so I^+(p) is contained in the second set; conversely, if a piecewise C^1 future causal path from p to q has a future timelike tangent, then (a) gives D in C^+, so q is in I^+(p); and no closed future causal path can have a timelike tangent because its displacement would have to lie in C^+ intersect {0}. (c) If p <= q and q <= p then q - p lies in Cbar^+ intersect (Cbar^-) = {0} by def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets, so p = q; a nonconstant closed future causal path would give D = 0 with nonconstant path, contradicting (a). (d) Apply (a) to the restriction of y to [a',b'] for arbitrary a' <= b'; the displacement has nonnegative time coordinate by (a) and the second clause of (a) with (b) of lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion gives strict positivity exactly for nonconstant restrictions. (e) Let x be an inertial chart and let v := D/T (in V), a future unit timelike vector with coordinates (v^0,v_s), v^0 > 0 and |v_s| < v^0 (lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion(a)); put beta := v_s/v^0 in R^3, so |beta| = |v_s|/v^0 < 1, and let B(beta) be the passive boost of def-lorentz-boost. Then B(beta)v = e_0: indeed B(beta) is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map (lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse, def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group), so B(beta)v is future unit timelike with time coordinate gamma(v^0 - beta . v_s) = gamma((v^0)^2 - |v_s|^2)/v^0 = gamma/v^0 = 1, since gamma = (1 - |beta|^2)^{-1/2} = v^0 by the unit identity, hence B(beta)v = e_0 and B(beta)D = T e_0. Let x_1 be the chart of the inertial frame whose ordered basis is e'_a := B(beta)^{-1} e_a (a valid eta-orthonormal, future and positively oriented basis because B(beta)^{-1} is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map, def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map, thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis): then x_1 = B(beta) o x up to translation and x_1(q) - x_1(p) = T e_0 with coordinates (T,0,0,0). The chart change is an affine map whose linear part is a Lorentz map, so it preserves eta: eta(y',y') = eta(y_1',y_1') for the coordinate paths, and it preserves the future direction of timelike tangents; hence y_1' is future timelike, its time coordinate is positive, and pointwise sqrt((y_1'^0)^2 - |y_1'_s|^2) <= y_1'^0 with equality exactly when y_1'_s = 0 (elementary inequality for 0 <= |b| <= a: sqrt(a^2 - b^2) <= a with equality iff b = 0). By lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability and def-sr-piecewise-proper-time, the finite improper-piece sum gives c Delta tau(y)=sum_i integral f_i<=sum_i integral y1'^0=x1^0(q)-x1^0(p)=T. Thus Delta tau(y)<=T/c, with exactly one conversion factor c^{-1}. Each integral is first taken on proper interior truncations and then passed to its finite endpoint limits. For equality put h_i=y1'^0-f_i>=0 on each open piece; it is continuous and dominated by y1'^0, hence improperly integrable. Equality forces every integral h_i to vanish. If h_i were positive at an interior point, continuity would give a compact interval with positive integral, contradicting that vanishing. Hence every spatial derivative vanishes on every open piece. Zero-derivative constancy and endpoint continuity give a constant spatial coordinate throughout; the positive time derivative makes the time coordinate strictly increasing, so y(s)=p+sigma(s)D with sigma continuous, strictly increasing and onto [0,1], C1 on open pieces and with finite positive one-sided quotient derivatives inherited from y. Conversely such a worldline has density T sigma', and its improper integral telescopes by the supplier lemma to T(sigma(b)-sigma(a))=T. This proves the bound and exact equality case for the approved weak class, retaining every straight attainment conclusion. (f) If F(p) = F(p_0) + L(p - p_0) with L proper orthochronous (def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group), then F(p + Cbar^+) = F(p) + L(Cbar^+) = F(p) + Cbar^+ because L preserves the future and past closed cones (thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra(iv)), which is exactly F(J^+(p)) = J^+(F(p)) and likewise for C^+ and I^+; the relation form follows. No choice principle is used: the arguments are finite-dimensional coordinate calculus, one explicit boost and ordinary integrals on compact interior truncations and finite improper endpoint limits.

consumer_interfaces.current_statement: Let $x$ be an inertial chart of the affine Minkowski model with coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, let $B:=\prod_{a=0}^{3}[c_a,d_a]$ with $c_a<d_a$ be a closed axis-parallel box, and let $T$ be a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on an open neighbourhood of $B$; put $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$ (continuous on $B$) as in [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]. (a) (Box identity.) For each $b$, with $F_a^+:=\{x\in B:x^a=d_a\}$, $F_a^-:=\{x\in B:x^a=c_a\}$ and each face integral the Riemann integral over the remaining three coordinates, $$\int_B f^b\,d^4x=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\Big(\int_{F_a^+}T^{ab}\,d^3x-\int_{F_a^-}T^{ab}\,d^3x\Big).$$ (b) (Slice balance.) Write $K:=\prod_{i=1}^{3}[c_i,d_i]$ and, for $s\in[c_0,d_0]$, $Q^b(s):=\int_K T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$; this is finite and continuous in $s$. For $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$, $$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K} f^b\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\Big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^+}T^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^-}T^{ib}\,d^3x\Big),$$ where $K_i^\pm$ are the two faces $x^i=d_i$, $x^i=c_i$ of $K$. (c) (Finite-flux conservation.) If $f=0$ on $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ and $T^{ib}=0$ on the side faces $[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^\pm$ for $i=1,2,3$, then $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$ for every $b$. The theorem concerns finite axis-parallel boxes in one inertial chart and is proved by the fundamental theorem of calculus. It does not assert a flux identity for arbitrary regions or hypersurfaces, does not assert that $Q^b$ transforms as a four-vector under a change of inertial chart, and asserts no conservation without the stated side-flux hypothesis; no noncompact or limiting statement is made. No choice principle is used.
consumer_interfaces.current_strategy: For (a): for fixed values of the remaining coordinates, $x^a\mapsto T^{ab}$ is $C^1$ on $[c_a,d_a]$, so one-variable FTC ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]) gives $\int_{c_a}^{d_a}\partial_aT^{ab}\,dx^a=T^{ab}(d_a)-T^{ab}(c_a)$; integrate this identity over the remaining three coordinates and sum over $a$, using Fubini/iterated integration for continuous functions on rectangles ([[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[cor-repeated-riemann-integrals-on-rectangles]]) and integrability of continuous functions on boxes ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]], [[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). For (b): apply (a) to the sub-box $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ and identify the first and last faces with $Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)$ and the spatial faces with the displayed side-flux terms; continuity of $Q^b$ follows quantitatively: the continuous $\partial_0T^{0b}$ is bounded by some $M$ on the box because continuous rectangle integrability includes boundedness ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]); FTC and the integral bound give $|Q^b(s)-Q^b(r)|\le\operatorname{Vol}(K)M|s-r|$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]). No choice principle is used.

consumer_interfaces.current_statement: In an inertial chart on all of affine Minkowski space define the smooth symmetric field $T^{00}=x^0$, $T^{01}=T^{10}=-x^1$, $T^{11}=x^0$, with every other component zero. Then $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ everywhere, since the only possibly nonzero divergence components are $\partial_0T^{00}+\partial_1T^{10}=1-1=0$ and $\partial_0T^{01}+\partial_1T^{11}=0$. For $L>0$, $c_2<d_2$, $c_3<d_3$, put $A=(d_2-c_2)(d_3-c_3)>0$ and $K=[0,L]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$. The full spatial slice integral is $Q^0(s)=\int_K T^{00}(s,x)\,d^3x=A Ls$. The axis-one side-flux difference on a slab $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ is $\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_1^+}T^{10}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_1^-}T^{10}\,d^3x=-A L(s_2-s_1)$; all transverse fluxes vanish. Consequently [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] gives $Q^0(s_2)-Q^0(s_1)=A L(s_2-s_1)\ne0$ whenever $s_1<s_2$. For example $A=6,L=2,s_2-s_1=3$ gives $36$. Thus zero local divergence alone does not conserve a finite slice integral: the side-flux/isolation hypothesis of the integrated-conservation theorem cannot be dropped. This prescribed tensor is not claimed to arise from any selected matter model.

Then D := q - p = (3,3,0,0) has eta(D,D) = -9 + 9 = 0 with D^0 = 3 > 0, so D is future null and q lies in J^+(p) but not in I^+(p) by the coordinate criterion; in particular the straight path from p to q is future null, not future timelike. Moreover no future timelike worldline y: [a,b] -> A with y(a) = p and y(b) = q exists: if it did, its displacement q - p would be future timelike by clause (a) of thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence, contradicting eta(D,D) = 0. The pair (p,q) is nonetheless causally related and the null straight segment realizes the relation, so the refuted statement is false.

consumer_interfaces.current_statement: Adopt the postulates post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and the causal signal restriction post-sr-causal-signal-propagation, and use the events, the relations <= and < and the sets J^+ and I^+ of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space together with the mathematical results lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion, lem-sr-spacelike-pairs-have-frame-dependent-time-order and thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence. Let x be the chart of any inertial frame with x^0 = c t (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart, def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions). Then, as conditional statements about the ideal model and not about any actual apparatus: (i) Receipt in the future light cone and absolute temporal order. If a signal is transmitted from p to q, then q is in J^+(p); if q is not p, then x^0(q) > x^0(p) and |x_s(q) - x_s(p)| <= x^0(q) - x^0(p) in every inertial chart, and every inertial frame's time order places the reception after the emission. Hence no inertial change of description reports the reception before the emission, and the temporal order of the endpoints of a transmission is the same in every inertial frame. (ii) Relay composition. If signals are transmitted from p to q and from q to r, then r is in J^+(p); if in addition q is in I^+(p) or r is in I^+(q), then r is in I^+(p). Thus relaying never leaves the causal future of the first emission and never returns to the emission event. (iii) No closed signal loop. If signals are transmitted from p to q and from q to p, then p = q; no chain of transmissions in this model returns to its own emission event. (iv) Frame independence of signal reachability. Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset of affine Minkowski space $A$, $c>0$, and let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field, $\eta(n,n)=-1$. Define the following first-order quantities in any inertial chart:
$$h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b,\qquad h_{ab}:=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b,\qquad a^b:=n^c\partial_cn^b,\qquad\theta_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\partial_{(c}n_{d)},$$
where symmetrization means half the sum, $n_a:=\eta_{ab}n^b$, and $h(v,w):=h_{ab}v^aw^b$. Here $h$ is $C^1$ and $a,\theta$ are continuous. The rest projection $h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$ is as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](c). For $C^1$ fields and tensors define
$$(L_nh)_{ab}:=n^c\partial_ch_{ab}+h_{cb}\partial_an^c+h_{ac}\partial_bn^c.$$
These first-order coordinate formulas transform tensorially under affine inertial chart changes and agree, on smooth fields, with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] and the ordinary smooth Lie derivative. Say the $C^1$ field is Born rigid when $L_nh=0$; the identity $L_nh=2\theta$ makes this equivalent to $\theta=0$.
(a) Let $J$ be a nonempty open interval, $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ a nonempty open set, and $\Phi:J\times B\to\Omega$ an injective $C^2$ immersion with $\partial_s\Phi=n(\Phi)$. Put $e_I:=\partial_{\xi^I}\Phi$, $I=1,2,3$, and $G_{IJ}(s,\xi):=h(e_I,e_J)$ at $\Phi(s,\xi)$. Then $n,e_1,e_2,e_3$ are linearly independent, $G$ is symmetric positive definite at every point, and its entries are $C^1$. Thus for each $s$ it is a $C^1$ positive-definite material metric on $B$. If $n$ and $\Phi$ are smooth, $G$ is a smooth Riemannian metric, as in the original smooth branch.
(b) For all $I,J$,
$$\partial_sG_{IJ}=(L_nh)(e_I,e_J)=2\theta(e_I,e_J),\qquad\partial_\tau G_{IJ}=2c\theta(e_I,e_J),$$
where $\tau=s/c$ is the proper-time parameter along each flow line, whose four-velocity is $cn$. For a nonzero label direction $e_I$, put $\ell_I:=\sqrt{h(e_I,e_I)}>0$ and $u_I:=h(e_I)/\ell_I$. This $u_I$ is a horizontal unit rest vector, and
$$\partial_\tau\ell_I=c\theta(u_I,u_I)\ell_I.$$
The alternative normalized material vector $e_I/\ell_I$ need not be horizontal, but has the same $\theta$ contraction because $\theta$ is horizontal. Positive/negative expansion gives positive/negative fractional change of this material rest length per proper time.
(c) If $\theta=0$, then $\partial_sG_{IJ}=0$ and $G_{IJ}(s,\xi)$ is constant in $s$ for each fixed label, with no restriction on material-label separation: the entire internal metric is preserved exactly. Conversely, a nonzero contraction $\theta(e_I,e_J)$ gives a nonzero derivative of that metric component at the point and hence nonconstancy on a neighborhood. The smooth Born-rigid branch and its original conclusions are included.
(d) This is a local statement about the given family and its material metric. Integrating the material metric at a common flow parameter gives an internal label-space length; it does not identify that length with a finite endpoint distance on a single observer's orthogonal simultaneity hyperplane without an additional argument. No matter model, elasticity, field equation, global rigidity theorem, boundary condition or choice principle is used.

$$2\theta_{ab}=\partial_an_b+\partial_bn_a+n_aa_b+a_an_b.$$
Differentiating $h_{ab}=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b$ in the displayed first-order Lie formula gives exactly this right side, proving $L_nh=2\theta$. The projectors make $\theta$ horizontal in both slots.
For the material fields, equality of the mixed partials of $C^2$ components of $\Phi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]) and the total chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) give
$$\partial_se_I^a=\partial_{\xi^I}n^a(\Phi)=(\partial_bn^a)(\Phi)e_I^b.$$

consumer_interfaces.current_statement: Consider the following hypothetical signalling model in the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (A,V,eta,C^+) with the SI coordinate conventions x^0 = c t (def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions). (S2) A received signal can be immediately re-emitted at the same event by a receiver, at speed u in the receiver's own rest frame (unrestricted receiving and relaying, no delay, no loss). (S3) Transmitters and receivers may move inertially at any speed v with 0 < v < c. (S4) The displacement between the emission and the reception event of a signal is a vector of the affine model, and displacements transform between inertial charts by the model's Lorentz transitions; the framework's kinematics is not modified. Then the following are exact identities of the model. (a) t(B_1) = L/(u - v) > 0 and x^1(B_1) = uL/(u - v) > 0, and the displacement B_1 - A_0 = (c t(B_1), x^1(B_1), 0, 0) is spacelike. consumer_interfaces.current_statement: Let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A. (i) Flow box. (1) Acceleration is not an additional aging term. In the model the reading of an ideal clock between two events of its history is the proper-time integral of its worldline (post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light (i), post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis (ii)); no term depending on the four-acceleration or any higher derivative of the history appears, and the clock hypothesis is precisely the exclusion of such terms. The corner of the piecewise inertial history is an idealization: a physical turnaround occupies a finite parameter interval, the worldline is then C^1 or smooth there, and its proper time is still the integral; the endpoint bound thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum still gives the comparison with the stay-at-home clock, and the strict inequality remains because such a smoothed itinerary still does not have the image of the straight segment. (2) The two histories are not symmetric in the model. One is the straight segment from p to q; the other contains the corner event r of texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion, and the three events p, r, q are not collinear. Every change of inertial chart is an affine bijection (lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz) and maps collinear triples to collinear triples; so no change of inertial frame maps the image of x_stay onto the image of x_travel or fixes both endpoints and exchanges the histories. The two twins are therefore not related by an inertial change of description, and the difference of readings is a model consequence of the different histories, not a consequence of who is 'really moving'. (3) The synchronization bookkeeping. In each momentary inertial rest frame of the traveler the stay-at-home clock runs slow by the factor 1/gamma, and the traveler may legitimately apply the time-dilation relation between events that are simultaneous in that momentary frame (lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas (i), def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance). But the two legs use different inertial frames: the outbound rest frame's simultaneity slice through the turn event r meets the stay-at-home worldline at the event with coordinate time t = T(1 - v^2/c^2) = T/gamma^2, while the inbound rest frame's slice through r meets it at t = T(1 + v^2/c^2); the two slices differ by 2Tv^2/c^2 in coordinate time, and inserting this gap reconciles the traveler's two leg-by-leg accounts of the stay-at-home clock with its total reading 2T at the reunion. The naive reciprocity statement 'each twin judges the other's clock to run slow' therefore compares different pairs of events for the two travelers (events simultaneous in different frames) and does not apply to the reunion comparison, which concerns the two clock readings at the single common event q. (4) Empirical qualification. All of (1)-(3) are conditional statements about ideal clocks in the adopted model; no measurement, apparatus, calibration, sampling or uncertainty model is involved, and no claim is made about real clocks or about nature. Real clock comparisons would additionally require apparatus and uncertainty analysis and are outside this remark.

$$M\ \ge\ \sum_{\text{massive legs }\ell\in S}m_\ell,$$
with equality if and only if $S$ is massive-only and every massive leg of $S$ has four-velocity $ce_0$ (all massive particles of that side at rest in the center-of-momentum frame).

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with $n:=e_0$, and let $x$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline whose chart coordinate path is $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$, with coordinate velocity $w:=r'$, coordinate acceleration $a:=w'$ and $\gamma:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; let $m>0$ be constant, $P:=mU$ with $U=\gamma(c,w)$ the four-velocity, $E:=E_n(P)$, $\mathbf p:=q_n(P)$ with coordinates $m\gamma w$, $F:=\dot P$ the four-force of [[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]] and $\mathbf f:=\frac{d}{dt}\mathbf p$ the coordinate three-force.
Then: (a) $F=mA$, where $A$ is the four-acceleration, and $\eta(P,F)=0$; equivalently $\eta(U,F)=0$ and the mass shell $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$ has vanishing proper-time derivative.
(b) $\frac{dE}{dt}=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$, the Euclidean inner product of the coordinate vectors.
(c) $F=\gamma\,(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\ \mathbf f)$, that is $F^0=\gamma\,\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c$ and $F^i=\gamma\mathbf f^i$ for $i=1,2,3$.
(d) If instead $m:I\to(0,\infty)$ is $C^1$ and $P=mU$ with this variable parameter, then $\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,\frac{dm}{d\tau}$; the constant-mass identities of (a) use the constancy of $m$ and must not be applied to variable-mass systems.

Since $\dot P=\gamma\,dP/dt$ and $dP/dt=(mc\gamma',m\gamma'w+m\gamma a)$, substituting gives (c). For (a), $\dot P=m\dot U=mA$ because $m$ is constant, and $\eta(U,A)=0$ by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(b); equivalently differentiate $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$ along the worldline. The chart coordinate velocity is dx^1/dt = c tanh theta, so |dx^1/dt| < c for every tau, and x^1 = R cosh theta > R|sinh theta| = |x^0| for every tau: the worldline lies in the right wedge W := {x^1 > |x^0|} and its speed in the chart tends to c only as tau -> +-infinity. (c) Rindler flow line. Let Phi(theta,rho,y,z) := (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2 and let n := rho^{-1} partial_theta be the Rindler congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), whose pullback metric is -rho^2 dtheta^2 + drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 and whose congruence acceleration a_cg := nabla_n n is rho^{-1} partial_rho, with eta(a_cg,a_cg) = rho^{-2} (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space, def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics). Along x one has x^1 - x^0 = R e^{-theta} -> 0 with x^0 -> +infinity as tau -> +infinity, and x^1 + x^0 = R e^{theta} -> 0 with x^0 -> -infinity as tau -> -infinity: the worldline approaches each of the null planes {x^1 = x^0} and {x^1 = -x^0} asymptotically without meeting either, and the chart coordinate speed tends to c at both ends. The curve is not asserted to be a geodesic and no statement is made about the forces that would maintain it. No choice principle is used.

Hence the two counter-propagating signals emitted at the same event reunite with the emitting material point at the reception events W_{phi_0}(t_1) and W_{phi_0}(t_2), each having gained exactly one circuit relative to that material point, and the chart-time difference of the two reunions is t_1 - t_2 = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2 R^2) > 0 for Omega > 0. The proper-time difference measured by the detector ideal clock is (t_1 - t_2)/gamma = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 sqrt(1 - Omega^2R^2/c^2)). Then, conditionally on the adopted model: (i) Frame data in x'. The data of the same covector k in x' is (omega',s') with omega' = gamma(1 - beta . s) omega > 0 and s' = [s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s) beta - gamma beta]/[gamma(1 - beta . s)] for beta nonzero (and omega' = omega, s' = s for beta = 0), so |s'| = 1 and k'_a = (-omega'/c, (omega'/c)s'_1, (omega'/c)s'_2, (omega'/c)s'_3) in x'. In the axis case beta = b e_1 with b in (-1,1): s'_1 = (s_1 - b)/(1 - b s_1) and (s'_2,s'_3) = (s_2,s_3)/(gamma(1 - b s_1)). (ii) Reading and frequency ratios. The rest observers of x and x' (four-velocities c e_0 and c e'_0) read angular frequencies omega = -c k(e_0) and omega' = -c k(e'_0); the linear frequencies and wavelengths of the two descriptions satisfy nu' = gamma(1 - beta . s) nu and lambda' = lambda/[gamma(1 - beta . s)]. More generally, an ideal observer whose coordinate velocity in x is w (a vector of the frame's spatial three-space with |w| < c) reads omega_o = gamma_w(1 - (w . s)/c) omega, where gamma_w := (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^(-1/2); equivalently omega_o = gamma_w(1 - beta_w . s) omega with beta_w := w/c. (iii) Longitudinal cases. If s = beta_hat then omega' = omega sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)) < omega, nu' = nu sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)) and lambda' = lambda sqrt((1 + |beta|)/(1 - |beta|)): the observer moving in the direction of propagation (away from a source at rest in x and located behind it) reads a red-shifted frequency and lengthened wavelength. If s = -beta_hat then omega' = omega sqrt((1 + |beta|)/(1 - |beta|)) > omega and lambda' = lambda sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)): blue shift for an observer moving opposite to the propagation direction (toward such a source). If beta . s = |beta|^2, equivalently s' . beta_hat = 0 (propagation direction perpendicular to the relative velocity in the frame x'), then omega' = omega/gamma < omega. Both configurations are called transverse Doppler configurations in the literature and the two factors differ; the direction and size of the shift are not determined by the word 'transverse' without specifying the frame in which transversality holds. (v) Aberration. If theta_x, theta_x' in [0,pi] are the angles between the propagation directions s, s' and the boost axis beta_hat, then cos theta_x' = (cos theta_x - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| cos theta_x); the map u |-> (u - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| u) is a strictly increasing bijection of [-1,1] onto itself, and in particular cos theta_x = 0 gives cos theta_x' = -|beta|. All clauses concern one ideal plane wave and ideal observers, and frequencies are compared through the phase model at specified reception events; the results are conditional on the adopted postulates (ideal plane wave, ideal clocks, inertial covariance, flat classical spacetime) and are not empirical claims about nature, sources or apparatus. They exclude media and dispersion, modulation and signal speeds, intensity and polarization, real line widths, accelerating observers (reserved to the framework's accelerated-observer page), gravitation and quantum effects; no statistical or measurement statement is made. If beta = 0 the two charts agree and omega' = omega, s' = s.

The rocket and thread-element worldlines are $x_\xi(t)=x^{-1}(ct,q(t)+\xi,y_0,z_0)$, with labels in an open interval $I$ containing $[0,L]$; the rockets are labels $0,L$.
(a) Every member is $C^2$ future timelike: its chart-time tangent is $(c,q\prime,0,0)$ with squared norm $-c^2/\gamma^2<0$. Its common proper-time function is $\tau(t):=\int_0^t\gamma(v)^{-1}dv$, and its proper four-velocity is $U=\gamma(c,q\prime,0,0)$ with squared norm $-c^2$. All members have equal chart velocity and acceleration, $q\prime,q\prime\prime$, and their chart separation is the constant $L$.
(b) The four-dimensional extension is essential for applying the material-family lemma. Choose open transverse intervals $Y,Z$ containing $y_0,z_0$, put $\sigma:=c\tau$, let $t=t(\sigma)$ be the inverse on $c\tau(J)$, and set
$$\Phi(\sigma,\xi,y,z):=x^{-1}(ct(\sigma),q(t(\sigma))+\xi,y,z),\qquad(\xi,y,z)\in B:=I\times Y\times Z.$$
This is an injective $C^2$ immersion onto an open set, with $dt/d\sigma=\gamma/c$ and $\partial_\sigma\Phi=n(\Phi)$, where $n=\gamma(1,\beta,0,0)$ is a $C^1$ future unit field. Apply the first-order definitions in [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]], which agree with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] when smooth. The longitudinal unit rest vector is $s_\parallel:=\gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$, and
$$\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=\gamma^3q\prime q\prime\prime/c^3.$$
This agrees with [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]](d), is nonzero exactly where $q\prime q\prime\prime\ne0$, and changes sign with that product. When $q$ is smooth the full original smooth-congruence branch is recovered. Restricting the extension to fixed $y_0,z_0$ gives the prescribed thread.
(c) For its material label tangent $e=\partial_\xi\Phi=(0,1,0,0)$, $h(e,e)=\gamma^2$ and $h(e)/\gamma=s_\parallel$. The vector $e/\gamma$ generally is not $s_\parallel$, but horizontality implies $\theta(e/\gamma,e/\gamma)=\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)$. The internal longitudinal material metric is $G_{11}=\gamma^2$, so its length at common flow parameter is
$$\mathcal L(t):=\int_0^L\sqrt{G_{11}}d\xi=\gamma(t)L.$$
It is an internal material metric length, not automatically the finite endpoint distance on one observer's orthogonal simultaneity hyperplane. The local evolution is
$$\frac{d}{d\tau}\log\mathcal L=c\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=\gamma^3q\prime q\prime\prime/c^2,\qquad\frac{d\mathcal L}{d\tau}=\gamma^4Lq\prime q\prime\prime/c^2.$$

(d) Under the stipulated material reading that thread elements follow these flow lines, the initial internal length is $\gamma(0)L$ and its relative factor is $\gamma(t)/\gamma(0)$. Relative to that initial state it stretches where $\gamma(t)>\gamma(0)$, shrinks where $\gamma(t)<\gamma(0)$, and has equal length where the factors agree. Equal chart-velocity and acceleration profiles in the translated family do not imply Born rigidity where $q\prime q\prime\prime\ne0$. Constant chart separation and constant internal rest metric are distinct kinematic conditions.
(f) This is a conditional flat-spacetime deduction for prescribed worldlines and the stated material reading. It assumes no dynamical or elastic model, force law, material failure criterion, measurement or empirical fact, and asserts nothing about real threads or rockets. No choice principle is used.

consumer_interfaces.current_statement: Adopt, on top of the flat spacetime postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], the SI conventions [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and the particle premises [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], the following classical continuum matter models on an open set $\Omega\subseteq A$: (i) Scalar field. A real smooth dimensionless field $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, a smooth potential $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with values in inverse square metres and a constant $K>0$ in joule per metre have the field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ -- the Euler-Lagrange equation of the adopted local action density, with stationarity defined by the finite relative action for compactly supported field variations ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]); the model's stress-energy tensor is the Hilbert tensor of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]. (ii) Dust. A $C^1$ rest energy density $\rho>0$ (joule per cubic metre) and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) satisfy $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the stress-energy tensor is $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$. (iii) Perfect fluid. $C^1$ fields $\varepsilon$ (energy density) and $P$ (pressure), both in joule per cubic metre, and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ satisfy the energy-balance and Euler equations of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; an equation of state or evolution equation determining $P$ is part of the model and is not supplied by this postulate; the stress-energy tensor is $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$. (iv) Additivity. The total stress-energy tensor of a composite system is the sum of the stress-energy tensors of its constituents (tensor-field addition on $\Omega$). (v) Adopted observer readings and units. For a tensor physically assigned to matter in this model, all inertial components $T^{ab}$ have units joule per cubic metre. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, an ideal observer with future unit direction $n$ and four-velocity $U=cn$ reads the numerical contractions of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] as energy density $\varepsilon_n=T^{ab}n_an_b$, momentum density $\pi_n^a=-c^{-1}h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$ and rest stress $S_n^{ab}=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}$. Here $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$. In an adapted inertial frame these are $T^{00}$, $T^{0i}/c$ and $T^{ij}$ respectively, and the energy-flux components are $cT^{i0}=c^2\pi_n^i$. Momentum density has units kilogram per square metre per second; energy flux has units watt per square metre; rest stress has units joule per cubic metre. These identifications are adopted model readings, not mathematical facts about an arbitrary symmetric tensor and not reported measurements. If $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ is assigned to external exchange, the spatial components $f^i$ are force per volume and $cf^0$ is power per volume: the corresponding numerical balances are $\partial_t(T^{00})+\partial_i(cT^{i0})=cf^0$ and $\partial_t(T^{0j}/c)+\partial_iT^{ij}=f^j$. Neither assignment selects a force law or asserts conservation. This postulate adopts model equations and tensor identifications only: it does not assert conservation of the tensors (that is derived from these equations in [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]), does not select any force law, interaction, equation of state, thermodynamic or dissipative behaviour, does not claim that these models exhaust physical matter, and contains no empirical premise, measurement or uncertainty statement.

consumer_interfaces.current_statement:
Adopt [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] and [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. Then the following conditional physical claims hold in the flat classical model, with the units of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]].
(a) Massive particle. Let a massive particle have constant mass $m>0$, four-momentum $P=mU$ and a future unit observer $n$. Its measured energy $E_n(P)=-c\eta(P,n)$, spatial momentum $q_n(P)=h(P)$ and kinetic energy $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ satisfy $E_n(P)>0$, $T_n(P)\ge0$ and the mass-shell identity $E_n(P)^2=m^2c^4+c^2|q_n(P)|^2$; $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if the particle is at rest in the observer's frame ($U=cn$). In an inertial frame whose stationary observer is $n=e_0$, the components are $P=(E/c,\mathbf p)$ with $E=E_{e_0}(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $\mathbf p=q_{e_0}(P)=m\gamma_w\mathbf w$ for the coordinate velocity $\mathbf w$, and under a passive boost the components transform as the components of the vector $P$; the combination $E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m^2c^4$ is frame-independent.
(b) Four-force. Along a $C^2$ worldline with four-acceleration $A$, the four-force $F=\dot P$ satisfies $\eta(P,F)=0$ and $F=mA$; in an inertial frame $F=\gamma\,(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\mathbf f)$ and $dE/dt=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$, where $\mathbf f=d\mathbf p/dt$ is the coordinate three-force. The constancy of $m$ is used; if instead $m$ is a $C^1$ variable mass parameter, then $\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,dm/d\tau$, and the constant-mass identities are not transferred to variable-mass systems.
(c) System mass. For a finite nonempty system of particles all of whose four-momenta are nonzero future causal and whose total four-momentum $Q$ is future timelike, the invariant mass $M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$ satisfies: in the center-of-momentum frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ one has $Mc^2=\sum_iE_{e_0}(P_i)$; every massive constituent has $E_{e_0}(P_i)\ge m_ic^2$, with equality exactly when it is at rest in that frame, and every massless constituent has $E_{e_0}(P_i)>0$. Hence $M\ge\sum_im_i$ over the massive constituents, with equality if and only if the system is massive-only and all its constituents are at rest in the center-of-momentum frame. If $Q$ is future null, then $M=0$, all constituents are massless with parallel momenta, and no center-of-momentum frame exists.
(d) Massless particle. An ideal massless particle has $E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$, has no rest frame and is not $mU$ for any $m>0$; it is not obtained from the massive formula by setting $m=0$.
(e) Necessary collision thresholds. Suppose that, under the adopted isolated-collision balance, an isolated collision occurs whose incoming legs are massive particles of constant masses $m_1,\dots,m_N$ and whose outgoing legs are massive particles of masses $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_K$ and possibly ideal massless particles. Let $M$ be the invariant mass of the common total four-momentum $Q$ when $Q$ is future timelike. Then the necessary inequalities $M\ge\sum_im_i$ and $M\ge\sum_j\mu_j$ hold; if the incoming side is a projectile of mass $m_1$ and a target of mass $m_2$ at rest in the observer frame of the target, with projectile energy $E$ and kinetic energy $T=E-m_1c^2$ in that frame, then
$$E\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^K\mu_j\Bigr)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2\Bigr],\qquad T\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^K\mu_j\Bigr)^2-(m_1+m_2)^2\Bigr],$$
and a single incoming massless particle cannot collide into an outgoing state containing a massive particle. These are kinematic necessity statements under the adopted conservation: they do not assert that any collision occurs, do not fix probabilities, amplitudes or cross sections, and are not empirical findings.
(f) Scope. All clauses are conditional on the two postulates and on the stated idealisations; the conclusions carry the same idealisations. No measurement, precision, statistical or empirical claim is made.

Adopt [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] (massive-particle momentum, the identification of measured quantities and isolated collision balance) and the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with stationary observer $n:=e_0$, spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ and inertial chart $x$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and let a massive particle have constant mass $m>0$ and four-momentum $P=mU$ with $U$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $y$ be a worldline of the particle whose inertial coordinate path is $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ and whose coordinate velocity $w(t)=r'(t)\in S$ of [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]\,(b) equals a fixed $w$ at the instant considered; then in this frame $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$ with $\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]]\,(b), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e)).

Fix $z_0\in[0,1)$ and suppose $z:=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$; put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, and let $N_p(m,w)=mw$ and $N_K(m,w)=\tfrac12m|w|^2$ be the Newtonian comparison quantities of [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]. With $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$ and $T_n(P)$ the measured energy, spatial momentum and kinetic energy identified in clause (ii) of the adopted postulate, $m(P)$ the invariant mass of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] and $R_E,R_q$ the remainders of [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-expansion-of-observer-quantities]]:

(a) [Energy] $E_n(P)=mc^2+N_K(m,w)+R_E$ and $E_n(P)-T_n(P)=mc^2$; $|R_E|\le K(z_0)\,z\,m|w|^2$. So the measured energy of the moving particle exceeds its rest energy by the Newtonian kinetic energy up to the displayed uniform bound of order $m|w|^4/c^2$.

(b) [Kinetic energy] $T_n(P)=N_K(m,w)+R_E$, hence $|T_n(P)-N_K(m,w)|\le 2K(z_0)\,z\,N_K(m,w)$: for $w\ne0$ the relative deviation from the Newtonian kinetic energy is at most $2K(z_0)z$.

(c) [Momentum] $q_n(P)=N_p(m,w)+R_q$, and $|R_q|\le\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0\bigr)z\,|N_p(m,w)|$; for $w\ne0$ the relative deviation from the Newtonian momentum is at most $(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0)z$.

(d) [Momentum-to-velocity inversion] $w=q_n(P)/(m\gamma_w)$ exactly, and $|w-q_n(P)/m|=(\gamma_w-1)|w|\le\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0\bigr)z\,|w|$; at $z=0$ one has $w=0$, $q_n(P)=0$, $E_n(P)=mc^2$ and $T_n(P)=0$, and $m(P)=m$ always.

(e) [Scope and uniformity] The constants $K(z_0)$ and $\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0$ depend on $z_0$ alone, so the estimates hold uniformly over all masses $m>0$, all states, instants and inertial frames with $|w|^2\le z_0c^2$. The statement is a conditional correspondence between the model's adopted measured quantities and the comparison functionals of a named frame: it identifies no framework with another, asserts no convergence of trajectories, forces or interactions and no limit in which the constant $c$ varies, gives no bound uniform in $|w|<c$ (see [[rem-sr-newtonian-bridge-limits-and-failures]]) and makes no empirical claim.

Let x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) be the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart) and let W := {x^1 > |x^0|} be the right wedge. Let Phi and n be the Rindler chart and congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b): Phi(theta,rho,y,z) = (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2 with inverse rho = sqrt((x^1)^2 - (x^0)^2), theta = (1/2) log((x^1+x^0)/(x^1-x^0)), pullback metric -rho^2 dtheta^2 + drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2, and acceleration field a_cg = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial_rho. Fix rho_0 > 0 and real y_0,z_0, and let O be the congruence worldline rho = rho_0, y = y_0, z = z_0, parametrized by its proper time tau with theta = c tau/rho_0; by def-sr-proper-acceleration its proper acceleration is c^2/rho_0. Write U(q) := q^0 + q^1 and V(q) := q^0 - q^1 for events q, so that U = rho e^{theta} and V = -rho e^{-theta} on W, and write <= and J^+, J^- for the causal reachability relations of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space. Then, conditionally on the adopted model: (i) Chart domain and light rays. Phi is a smooth bijection of R x (0,inf) x R^2 onto W with the stated smooth inverse, so the chart domain is exactly W and rho = 0 is not part of its coordinate domain. The boundary of W in the affine model is {x^1 = |x^0|}, with arbitrary x^2,x^3: it is the union of the two null half-planes {x^1 = x^0 >= 0} and {x^1 = -x^0 >= 0}. These half-planes are portions of the full null planes appearing as causal horizons in (ii); the full planes are not the wedge boundary. Along the worldline rho = rho_0 one has V = -rho_0 e^{-theta} -> 0^- and U -> +infinity as theta -> +infinity, while U = rho_0 e^{theta} -> 0^+ and V -> -infinity as theta -> -infinity. The future null straight lines of the model that lie in the plane y = y_0, z = z_0 and meet O are exactly the lines of constant V (on which dtheta = +drho/rho) and the lines of constant U (on which dtheta = -drho/rho). (ii) Causal horizons. An event q satisfies q <= p for some event p of O if and only if V(q) < 0; an event q satisfies p <= q for some event p of O if and only if U(q) > 0. Consequently no event with V(q) >= 0 can ever influence O; this set contains the null plane {x^1 = x^0}, the left wedge {x^1 < -|x^0|} and the future wedge {x^0 > |x^1|}; and no event with U(q) <= 0 can ever be influenced by O, a set containing the null plane {x^1 = -x^0}, the left wedge and the past wedge {x^0 < -|x^1|}. The null plane {x^1 = x^0} is the boundary of the causal past of O (the future horizon: the surface its worldline approaches as theta -> +infinity), and the null plane {x^1 = -x^0} is the boundary of the causal future of O (the past horizon); every event of the left wedge is causally unrelated to O in both directions. The same criteria with O any other congruence worldline rho = rho_1, y = y_1, z = z_1 hold verbatim: the constants rho_0, y_0, z_0 do not enter. (iii) Radar time and distance to a coaxial congruence reflector. Fix rho_m > 0 with rho_m != rho_0 and let R_m be the congruence worldline rho = rho_m, y = y_0, z = z_0 (a second uniformly accelerated observer, coaxial with O, with proper acceleration c^2/rho_m). Let e_- be the event of O at parameter theta_e (so tau(e_-) = rho_0 theta_e/c up to the base point of tau), let q_m be the event of R_m lying on the future null straight line from e_- in the plane y = y_0, z = z_0, and let e_+ be the event of O lying on the future null straight line from q_m; the reflection at q_m is idealized as instantaneous and as leaving R_m's motion unchanged, as in def-sr-operational-radar-protocol. Then e_-, q_m, e_+ exist uniquely, the Rindler time of q_m is theta_m = theta_e + |log(rho_m/rho_0)|, the return event satisfies theta(e_+) = theta_e + 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)| and (theta_e + theta(e_+))/2 = theta_m, so the round trip lasts 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)| in Rindler time and (2rho_0/c)|log(rho_m/rho_0)| in O's proper time. The radar protocol therefore assigns to q_m the radar time tau_rad(q_m) = (rho_0/c) theta_m plus the base constant of tau and the radar distance rho_rad(q_m) = rho_0 |log(rho_m/rho_0)|; within this coaxial family the radar-time level sets are exactly the Rindler simultaneity slices theta = const, i.e. the rest slices of the congruence (def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance). The radar distance is not the rest distance: in the slice theta = theta_m the two worldlines are at rest distance |rho_m - rho_0|, whereas for rho_m = 2rho_0 the radar distance is rho_0 log 2 < rho_0, because log is strictly increasing and e > 2 implies log 2 < log e = 1 (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws); For every distinct positive reflector radius the notions differ: with $r=\rho_m/\rho_0$, one has $\log r<r-1$ when $r>1$ and $-\log r>1-r$ when $0<r<1$. The two distance formulas agree only at $r=1$, where both have the continuous degenerate value zero. The coincident case is not a nonzero emission-reflection-reception triple of the protocol, whose distinct-reflector hypothesis remains in force. As rho_m -> 0^+ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration c^2/rho_m diverges; as rho_m -> +infinity the round-trip proper time and the radar distance also grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration tends to 0. (iv) Restrictions of the protocol. No event with V >= 0 - in particular no event of the horizon plane {x^1 = x^0}, of the left wedge or of the future wedge - can be assigned a radar time or radar distance by this protocol from O, because by (ii) it cannot causally precede any reception event on O: the required reflection-to-reception leg is impossible. Separately, every event with U <= 0 lacks an emission-to-reflection leg from O. Thus any event admitting this radar triple must satisfy U > 0 and V < 0, equivalently it must belong to W; the horizon is at infinite radar distance in the limit rho_m -> 0^+. For example q = x^{-1}(2rho_0,0,y_0,z_0) has U(q)=V(q)=2rho_0>0. It is causally after O at theta=0, since the displacement is (2rho_0,-rho_0,0,0), future timelike, and it even lies on a future null ray from O at theta=log 2, with displacement (5rho_0/4,-5rho_0/4,0,0). Nevertheless it cannot send a causal return to O, so receives no radar assignment from O. The protocol therefore does not extend to a global coordinate system of A. (v) Scope. All clauses are conditional computations and readings in flat classical spacetime with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors, for the specified congruence worldlines. They are not empirical claims and contain no measurement, apparatus, source, detector or statistical content; gravitation, media, dispersion, finite resolution, quantum effects and material models of the reflector are excluded. No choice principle is used.

(a) Units in the adopted coordinates x^0 = c t: the phase theta is dimensionless; the coordinates x^a, the wavelength lambda and all distances are in metres; the components k_a of a wave covector, the wave vector kappa and varpi = -k(e_0) are in m^-1; the angular frequencies omega and omega_n and the linear frequencies nu are in s^-1 (nu also in hertz); c is in m s^-1; and s, beta, beta_w and gamma are dimensionless. (b) Two coordinate forms. In the adopted coordinates theta = -omega t + kappa . x_vec + const and k_a = (-omega/c, (omega/c)s); in a chart whose time coordinate is t in seconds directly, so that the metric component g_tt = -c^2 carries m^2 s^-2 and the time-space components carry m s^-1, the same phase is theta = -omega t + kappa . x_vec + const with the same omega and kappa, and the component tuple (-omega, (omega/c)s) carries mixed units; formulas derived in one convention are not reused unchanged in the other. This is the general warning of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions specialized to the wave covector. (c) Natural units and restoration. The dimensionless factors gamma(1 - beta . s) and the longitudinal square roots need no c restoration because they contain only beta, s and gamma; the c restoration affects the map between omega, nu, lambda and the components of k, not the shift factors themselves. (d) This remark introduces no quantum identification of energy with hbar omega, no amplitude or intensity content and no measurement claim; it is a units and convention statement carrying the scope of the items it cites.

consumer_interfaces.current_statement: Statement refuted: 'In the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space with the inertial chart x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3), the null plane H := {x^1 = x^0}, is a boundary of the model in the following three senses: (i) no future causal curve crosses from {x^1 > x^0} to {x^1 < x^0}; (ii) H separates all causal relations, so no event of {x^1 > x^0} is causally related to any event of {x^1 < x^0}; and (iii) the metric degenerates on H, so that H is a singular boundary of the spacetime on which the model fails.' Here H is the full causal-past boundary of the accelerated congruence; only its half-plane {x^1 = x^0 >= 0} belongs to the boundary of the right wedge W={x^1>|x^0|}. Counterexample: (a) A future timelike crossing refutes the causal separation claims. Let p := x^{-1}(-1,0,0,0) and q := x^{-1}(3,1,0,0), and let y: [0,1] -> A be the affine segment y(s) := p + s(q-p). The displacement q - p has chart components (4,1,0,0), so eta(q-p,q-p) = -16 + 1 = -15 < 0 and the time component is 4 > 0: the segment is a future timelike curve (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). Its coordinate function x^0 - x^1 takes the values -1 at s = 0 and +2 at s = 1, hence vanishes at s = 1/3, at x^{-1}(1/3,1/3,0,0): a future timelike curve crosses H, refuting (i). Moreover q is in the causal future of p in the sense p <= q of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space, and p and q lie on opposite sides of H, so the segment relates events on opposite sides, refuting (ii). (b) Events of H and of its complement are causally related in both directions. The event r := x^{-1}(0,1,0,0) satisfies r < x^{-1}(1,1,0,0) because the displacement (1,0,0,0) is future timelike; and x^{-1}(1,1,0,0) < x^{-1}(2,3/2,0,0) because the displacement (1,1/2,0,0) satisfies -1 + 1/4 < 0 with positive time component (lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion (c)). The event x^{-1}(1,1,0,0) lies on H while r and x^{-1}(2,3/2,0,0) do not, so H neither separates causal relations nor consists of causally isolated events. (c) No metric degeneracy occurs. In the inertial chart the matrix of eta is the constant diag(-1,1,1,1) on the whole model, hence eta is nondegenerate and constant everywhere, in particular on H; and the actual crossing event x^{-1}(1/3,1/3,0,0) on the future timelike segment of (a) is an event of H on which the metric is the ordinary flat metric. It occurs at parameter 1/3, not at the midpoint of that segment. The Rindler map Phi(theta,rho,y,z) = (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) with theta in R and rho > 0 is, by thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), a smooth bijection onto W with a smooth inverse; its domain simply satisfies rho > 0, so its coordinate domain omits rho = 0 and its image omits H; the wedge boundary consists only of the two null half-planes x^1 = |x^0| >= 0, whereas H is one of the full causal-horizon planes, and the failure of the map to be defined there is a property of the coordinate map, not of eta. (d) An inertial worldline crosses H. The worldline z(t) := x^{-1}(c t, 0, 0, 0) of the inertial frame satisfies z(0) = x^{-1}(0,0,0,0), which lies on H, and is defined and future timelike for every real t; thus a single regular worldline passes through H from the region x^1 > x^0 (for t < 0 it has x^1 = 0 > x^0 = c t) to the region x^1 < x^0 (for t > 0), which refutes (i) in a second way and contradicts the reading of H as a boundary on which the model fails. What remains true is exactly the conditional statement of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (ii), that the specific congruence worldlines cannot be reached from events with V >= 0; this is a restriction of causal reachability of those worldlines and not a boundary or singularity of the affine model. (e) Scope. All assertions are mathematical statements about the affine model and its causal reachability relations; no physical interpretation, measurement or empirical claim is made, and no choice principle is used.

consumer_interfaces.current_statement: Adopt as the boundary and isolation premise of the continuum framework: (i) Total tensor. In every conservation or integration statement of this framework the tensor used is the total stress-energy tensor of the system considered, including every constituent that carries energy-momentum -- matter, fields and supporting structures present in the region -- assembled by the additivity clause of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]]. (ii) Localisation. Whenever conservation of a slice four-momentum over a coordinate-time interval $[s_1,s_2]$ is asserted in an inertial chart, the model assumes that during that interval the total tensor is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of a closed box $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$, that its components satisfy the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces of the box for $i=1,2,3$, and that the slice integrals converge; equivalently, the system is isolated inside the chosen region for the chosen interval. (iii) Failure of isolation. If the side flux does not vanish, only the exact finite-flux balance of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] is asserted; no conservation of a slice integral is inferred and no limiting procedure at spatial infinity is adopted. (iv) Unmodelled matter. For a matter system not governed by one of the models of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]], conservation of its stress-energy tensor is not inferred; if used it must be adopted or derived separately. (v) Exclusion caution. Removing a constituent -- a support, a field or a container -- from the total tensor can make the side-flux condition fail; the premise concerns the total tensor of the system, not an arbitrary partial tensor. This premise is an idealisation of an isolated bounded system in flat spacetime; it is not a measurement and makes no apparatus, statistical or empirical claim.

Scope remark on the limits of the low-speed bridge. Each quantitative assertion is an immediate consequence of the cited displayed identities; none of them is used as a premise elsewhere on this page.

(i) [No speed-independent error constant] Let $m>0$. For every $B\ge0$ there are a future unit $n\in V$, a vector $U$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and a state $P=mU$ whose relative velocity $w$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d) satisfies $|w|<c$ and $\bigl|T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2\bigr|>B$, with $T_n$ as in [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]. Explicitly, for every integer $\gamma\ge2$ there is such a state with Lorentz factor $\gamma$, namely $|w|=c\sqrt{1-\gamma^{-2}}$, for which [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ while $\tfrac12m|w|^2=\tfrac12mc^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$, so $$T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2=mc^2\Bigl(\gamma-\tfrac32+\tfrac{1}{2\gamma^2}\Bigr)\to\infty\quad(\gamma\to\infty),$$ and the relative deviation from the Newtonian value equals $\frac{(2\gamma+1)(\gamma-1)}{\gamma+1}\to\infty$. Consequently the constants $K(z_0)$ and $\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0$ of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] necessarily depend on the speed bound $z_0$, no bound of that form is uniform on the whole domain $|w|<c$, and $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$ and $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}$ are unbounded as $|w|\to c$ although $\tfrac12m|w|^2\le\tfrac12mc^2$ there.

(ii) [The massless case is excluded, not a limit] An ideal massless particle of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]] carries a nonzero future null four-momentum $P$ and, by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(i), satisfies $E_n(P)=c|q_n(P)|>0$ exactly; it has no four-velocity, proper time or relative velocity, and no rest mass, rest energy or kinetic energy is assigned to it. The hypotheses $m>0$ and $z\le z_0<1$ exclude it, and no substitution $w$ with $|w|=c$ is available because $\gamma_w$ is undefined there. The bridge therefore concerns massive particles only, and it neither derives nor constrains the ideal massless case or light.

(iii) [Bounded chart regions, not a limit of frameworks] The uniform chart statement [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]] holds on each bounded region $D_{T,R}$ and fails on unbounded regions (its clause (d)); the correspondence is a conditional statement about the adopted model in a bounded low-speed domain, and it is neither an equivalence between the relativistic and Newtonian frameworks, nor a physical process in which the constant $c$ varies, nor empirical evidence for either framework. The Newtonian comparison quantities [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]] are comparison expressions, not the derived quantities of a separate theory.
